mechanisms: Financial viability is the binding constraint: if a tool adds cost to a grant-dependent household, it is rejected regardless of pedagogical promise.
A conducive home environment is non-negotiable: without quiet and space, e-learning is dismissed as less effective than contact classes.

Pedagogical fit is judged by interactivity: tools that match digital-native preferences for speed, graphics, and instant rewards are valued and perceived as transformative, though perception does not guarantee sustained usage.
Role threat blocks adoption: when instructors see a tool as a replacement rather than a teaching aid, they confine it to administrative tasks.
Infrastructure deficits poison attitudes: slow internet and computer shortages breed frustration that extinguishes engagement before content is even tried.
objection_patterns: Will this add to the financial burden my household already carries?
Do I have a quiet, private space to use this properly?
Does this tool replace my teacher, or does it help them teach?
Will this even work on our slow internet and shared computers?
